newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Pininfarina in China vehicle joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Pininfarina in China vehicle joint venture.

text.p: Italian car designer Pininfarina and China's Hafei Motor Co said on Wednesday they had signed a joint venture to produce a new multi-purpose vehicle for international markets.
Hafei managing director Cui Xuewen told a news conference that design work on the project had already started at Pininfarina's headquarters in the northern city of Turin.
Production development will shift to Hafei's factories in China in 1997. The vehicles are expected to start rolling off the assembly lines towards the end of 1998.

"This is the first time that a Chinese company has joined forces with a foreign company to produce a new vehicle," Xuewen said. Hafei is controlled by Harbin Aircraft Manufacture Corp and is the ninth biggest automobile maker in China.
Negotiations over the joint venture took two years to complete and Pininfarina chief executive Sergio Pininfarina told reporters he hoped the initial deal would develop further.
"This is only the first stage of our partnership, which will last a long time and see us working with Hafei in a Chinese market which has enormous potential," he said.
Pininfarina is a family-controlled business, which has helped design many cars for the Fiat group.
Xuewen said the new vehicle would be multi-functional, "good both for families and companies". He added that he expected production capacity of some 80,000 vehicles a year.

"It will be a low-cost, high quality product aimed at the Chinese, Asian and African markets," he told reporters, adding that Pininfarina and Hafei were already thinking about working on another project.
"We hope that a second generation car could be exported to Europe," he said.
Neither company would give financial details of the accord, but Pininfarina said it was a large investment for his firm.
"We are not expecting spectacular profits," he said, indicating that the value of the deal lay in the fact that his company was gaining a place in the fast-growing Chinese market.
